_meta.purpose: REGRESSION baseline, not a correctness claim -- see tests/test_golden_pipeline.py's module docstring. PRIMARY mode (ekf_auto_pacejka, production default since 2026-09-01): the underlying tyre curve is fit fresh on this data every time modules.tyre_fit_auto.fit_session_pacejka runs -- this golden pins CURRENT fit-chain output, not a frozen prior-session curve.

stability_estimation._comment_cs_window_floors: CS window floors: cs_min_window_s = 0.1 s, the chair's own value, unchanged. Tested 0.2 s against it on real data (100 Hz grid): same results on all 14 corners, no bootstrap difference -> no reason to deviate. Bootstrap spread measures precision, not closeness to the true tangent; floors chosen by direct validation.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py + inspect_cs_duration_only_comparison.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Exactly the chair's own literal default (10 samples @ their 100 Hz = 0.1s), zero deviation, now that the 100 Hz grid supplies the sample count that default always assumed. A 0.2s hypothesis (double the chair's value, motivated by an a priori 'this car's alpha comes from an ESTIMATED beta -- kinematic or EKF/auto-fit, a noisier Level 1-3 chain -- vs the chair's own MEASURED beta channel, so more averaging seemed plausible') was TESTED AND REJECTED, not just superseded: an isolated duration-only bootstrap (span held at 0.02 rad, cornering-only population) found 0.1s and 0.2s statistically indistinguishable at every tested phase length, and direct real-data validation confirmed the two floors reproduce the SAME worst-lap population almost exactly (identical negative-corner counts, same corners flagged, C4 rear even reads a stronger negative at 0.1s). The plausible-sounding physical story was not supported by either form of evidence gathered -- recorded honestly rather than left implied.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_samples_floor_derived_from: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.2s*20Hz=4 samples would round below a robust minimum; floored at 5 (same magnitude as cs_phase_min_valid_samples's own robustness reasoning), mirroring modules.longitudinal_stiffness's own min_samples_floor precedent.
stability_estimation.cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Rate-independent (alpha-domain, radians) -- no sample-rate correction applies. Reverted from attempt 2's falsified 0.01 rad back to 0.02 rad (the chair's own original span) after direct real-data validation; unaffected by the separate cs_min_window_s duration question (0.2s vs 0.1s) -- span was never the axis in question there.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_max_window_m: Locality cap for CS window growth, in track metres (state['s_m']), not samples -- same meaning in slow and fast corners. Natural window on corner samples: median 24.1 m front / 35.4 m rear (diagnostics/inspect_cs_max_window_locality_sizing.py); cap = 1.5 x rear median = 53 m. No corner lost at either floor (diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py). The span floor, not min_window, sets the real window size. Limitation: some corner-to-corner gaps are < 53 m, so a window can bridge into a neighbour there. Floors not met within the cap -> NaN.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_phase_min_valid_samples: Per-phase CS_ratio median -> NaN below this many finite samples. 5 = smallest n where the median isn't just one or two extreme readings. Generic backstop; apex_3 handled by apex_region.
stability_estimation._comment_ls_phase_min_valid_samples: Same gate for ls_ratio_f/r, own key (LS noise differs from CS). Same criterion, same value.
stability_estimation._comment_stab_phase_no_braking_floor_bar: entry_1_brake stability stat: same sample-count gate as CS (cs_phase_min_valid_samples), plus no signal if max brake_f_bar never exceeds this floor (no real braking). v3 log_pbrake_f at throttle > 90%: 32829 samples, p99 = 0 bar, one 6.03 bar transient (diagnostics/inspect_v3_brake_phase_stability.py). Real braking phases >= 13.6 bar. 3.0 bar sits between.
stability_estimation.cs_linear_slip_threshold_rad_derived_fro: diagnostics/inspect_cs_window_floor_derivation.py, linear_region_end, 2026-09-02 (CS validity repair). Binned the session's own Fy-vs-alpha cloud (both axles, folded to a single sign via the tyre curve's expected odd symmetry, moving & non-kerb samples) with sliding 0.04-rad-wide windows (matched to the re-derived cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad, not an arbitrary narrow bin -- a narrower bin reproduces the same small-span sampling noise the N/span sweeps diagnosed) stepped by 0.005 rad, comparing each window's local slope against the near-origin reference window ([0,0.04) rad). Departure stays within +/-15% of the reference out to ~0.03 rad on both axles, then exceeds 10% and STAYS exceeded (not a single noisy crossing) from window leading edge 0.045 rad (front) / 0.035 rad (rear) onward, climbing to full sign reversal by ~0.08-0.09 rad -- the genuine nonlinear/saturation region. Value set at the more conservative (earlier-onset) axle's sustained-departure point, 0.035 rad, rounded down slightly to 0.03 rad for a safety margin against measurement noise; both axles' own curves are still flat (within a few % of the reference) at 0.03 rad.
stability_estimation._comment_grid_rate: Common grid = min(target_sample_rate_hz, slowest native rate of the fast CS channels: sclu_yaw_rate, log_asteer, log_acc_y, log_acc_z, lap_distance). On Dubai those are 100 Hz, ecu_speed 50 Hz (diagnostics/inspect_native_channel_rates.py); ecu_speed upsampled linearly (inertia-limited). Below min_sample_rate_hz -> refused, naming the binding channel; exactly 50 Hz -> runs, status 'channel-limited'. Known limits: tyre_model_ekf.pass_1's R was calibrated on the old 50 Hz grid; nis_window_samples (nis_gate/tyre_fit_auto/tyre_model_ekf) and apex_half_window_samples are still sample counts -> half their calibrated duration at 100 Hz. [2026-10-03: kerb_dilation_samples removed from this list -- replaced by the time-based kerb_dilation_s (Q-CAL-1 option 0).]
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source: Which beta feeds Modules 4b/5. Default 'ekf_auto_pacejka' (per-session fit, gated, kinematic fallback). 'kinematic' = estimate_sideslip, the universal fallback. 'ekf_pass_1' = frozen Dugoff curve with calibrated noise (sideslip_ekf_dugoff.py). Traces are fine under any source; verdict thresholds are calibrated for thresholds_calibrated_for_sideslip_source only -> [UNCAL] banner otherwise.
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source_auto_modes: 'ekf_auto_dugoff' / 'ekf_auto_pacejka': fit this session's tyre curve (tyre_fit_auto), run the NIS gate, use the EKF's beta_with_fallback only if gate = pass/warn and fit not degenerate; else kinematic, recorded as fallback_used/fallback_reason. Thresholds are never calibrated for these -> [UNCAL] always. ekf_auto_dugoff is experimental: selectable via this key only, removed from the UI selector 2026-09-30 (it falls back to kinematic on every run on this car).
stability_estimation._comment_vertical_load_source: 'static' = estimate_vertical_loads' static/aero/transfer model. 'measured' = wheel_loads cascade (damper -> axle-total reconstruction -> static) for the Fz used by fy_norm and the tyre fit. No damper channels (e.g. Dubai) -> every corner invalid -> cascade returns static everywhere, identical by construction.
stability_estimation.vertical_load_source_derived_from: DEFAULT FLIPPED to 'measured' 2026-09-04 (user decision) -- verdict independence PROVEN, not assumed, before the flip: CS_ratio/stability (the only classification/verdict inputs) never receive fz as an argument at all (code-level: estimate_cornering_stiffness/estimate_yaw_moment_stability's own signatures) and both run BEFORE fz is computed in the pipeline; empirically confirmed on Dubai -- fz_f_N differed by up to 8591.8N between static and measured, but CS_ratio_f/CS_ratio_r/C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r/stability_observed_Nm_per_deg were BYTE-IDENTICAL. The flip therefore carries ZERO classification/verdict risk by construction -- it only changes fy_f_norm_N/fy_r_norm_N (display) and the Phase-2 diagnostic mu tyre-fit's own load input, both display/diagnostic quantities. tests/test_vertical_load_source_default.py confirms the live default is 'measured' and resolves correctly both with real damper channels present (measured cascade engages, every corner tier=damper) and without any (falls back automatically, numerically identical to an explicit 'static' run).
stability_estimation._comment_gps_course_anchor: estimate_sideslip_gps (validation only) anchor gate: smoothed |ay| < max_ay_g for >= min_duration_s. Raw per-sample |ay| gave only ~0.1 s runs; smooth_window_s 0.3 -> 6 runs >= 1.5 s on Dubai. max_ay_g 0.05 ~ moving |ay| p10 (0.044 g), before the rise toward cornering (p20 0.109 g). diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py.
stability_estimation.gps_course_latency_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py (GPS-course sideslip validation, 2026-07-26): cross-correlation of wrap-safe d(course)/dt against -yaw_rate_radps over lags -1..+1s (racing laps, moving samples) peaks at r=0.9898 at lag=+0.32s, vs r=0.9575 at zero lag -- course-derived rotation consistently lags yaw_rate by this much. A stale course reading recorded at time t describes the vehicle's true state at (t - latency); querying it at (t + latency) recovers the value that actually corresponds to the query instant.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_apex_region: apex_3 = one instant +/- apex_half_window_samples (11 samples) -- can't clear the CS window floor. apex_region = +/- cs_apex_region_half_length_m around the apex position, used for apex_3 CS reads in classification; apex_3 unchanged otherwise. 25 m = half the ~20-40 m extent of the C4 CS dip -> inside one event, short of the next straight or corner.
stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal); values = the chair's defaults. Changing any of the six means re-deriving the classification thresholds.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_fallback: Fallback C_linear_ref: axle load x C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 (Milliken RCVD, GT3 slick). Front (290+290)*9.81*12 = 68268, rear (395+381)*9.81*12 = 91343. Level 1. Only used as the fixed stiffness prior of diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py; no production consumer. [2026-10-03 CORRECTION, text only, no value change (PLAN.md section 7 note 7b, Q-PUSH exit ruling 1): the same C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 on both axles implies a NEUTRAL-STEER car (K = 0). The measured understeer gradient is K2 = +1.27 to +1.41 deg/g (understeer; Q-PUSH P1, Rajamani Eq. 3.23 regression, three sessions) -- named as the measured replacement candidate (Q-K2).]
stability_estimation.kerb_dilation_s_derived_from: Q-CAL-1 option 0, author ruling 2026-10-03 (neutral engineering, unit repair). Replaces kerb_dilation_samples = 5, which was set as 100 ms each side on the old fixed 50 Hz grid and silently ran as +/-50 ms after the grid moved to 100 Hz (formerly a known limit in _comment_grid_rate). Restores the calibrated +/-100 ms; samples = round(kerb_dilation_s x grid rate) at runtime, so the physical padding is the same at 50 and 100 Hz. Premise check: diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py, thesis_notes 'Q-CAL-1 measurement'.
stability_estimation.kerb_smear_grade_s_derived_from: Q-CAL-1 option 4, author rulings 2026-10-03. Grade-zone width of the near_strike mark: a CS window [start, i) holding a sample within this time of a kerb-mask sample (outside the mask, either side) carries the mark. Flag only -- no exclusion, no down-rank, no verdict change. The 2 Hz zero-phase CS filter runs before the mask and spreads a strike into unmasked neighbours; diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py measured the Fy smear past the edge at p75 = 0.25 s (15 NBR + 2 Paul Ricard sessions) and the coincidence count shows the deep-CS enrichment ending there (rear ends ~250 ms; front 250-360 ms band adds only x1.7). GEOMETRY: that 0.25 s was measured from the OLD +/-50 ms mask edge; the restored +/-100 ms dilation (kerb_dilation_s) moves the edge out by 50 ms, so 0.20 s from the new edge keeps the same measured physical boundary. One value, both axles (no front/rear difference in the Fy smear). Tier B.

classification._comment: Corner-verdict thresholds for _classify_corner. Each derived_from names the run and estimator it was picked on -- valid only for that distribution; re-derived per estimator/car, never taken from the chair.
classification.cs_cross_lap_aggregation_note: modules/recommendation.py aggregate_by_corner: 'median' (pre-2026-09-02 default) or 'worst_lap' (min-then-min, worst phase of worst lap). Ships atomically with the STRONG/MODERATE_CS* thresholds above, which were derived against the worst_lap population -- do not flip back to 'median' without re-deriving those four values against the median population first.

stab_neg_thresh_Nm_per_deg.derived_from: 2026-10-05, author ruling: Werner 2021 sec. 2.2.3 sign criterion as the anchored boundary -- dMz/dbeta < 0 is open-loop unstable; explicitly not a criticality threshold (skilled drivers operate there), so the verdict reads 'open-loop unstable (Werner)' and its severity stays contextual (two-signal logic). Measure chair-conform (inertial regressand, default (c)). Clean-pool worst-phase distribution beside (inspect_threshold_rederivation.py counts_clean): n 109, 9 negative, p5 -5 / p10 +27 / p15 +50 Nm/deg. Supersedes -50.0 (2026-07-24, kinematic-era placeholder, never re-derived for ekf_auto_pacejka), retired 2026-10-05. [2026-10-06: the product text reads 'open-loop unstable' -- no source names in the app (author ruling); the anchor stays here and in PRODUCTION.md.]

verdict_stability_margin.derived_from: 2026-09-19, verdict sensitivity sweep (diagnostics/inspect_metrology_phase1_sensitivity.py). Not a threshold -- a MARGINAL annotation ui/views/outing_form.py's _classify_corner appends to its own verdict when the axle value actually driving that verdict sits within cs_margin of the nearest STRONG/MODERATE_CS* threshold. 0.11 is the empirical threshold-distance of the 2nd-most-marginal corner-phase that actually flipped under a real +/-1% perturbation of mass/front_fraction/wheelbase/yaw_inertia/steering_ratio (v3 C12 apex_3/exit_4, distance 0.104, rounded up slightly), covering 9 of the 10 observed flips. The one excluded case (Dubai C1 apex_3, distance 0.274) was read directly and found to be a different mechanism (which of CSf/CSr is currently more extreme, a relative front/rear comparison _classify_corner also makes, not a fixed-threshold crossing) -- inflating this margin to cover it would flag far more corners than the sweep supports. TWO-SESSION CAVEAT, stated not hidden: this anchor is derived from exactly two real sessions (Dubai, GT3_PRC_MLA-v3) -- re-check it once a third session's own sensitivity sweep is available, the same standing caveat every single/two-session-derived threshold in this block already carries (STRONG/MODERATE_CSF/CSR above are also single-session). [2026-10-05: re-measured on the corrected chain, wheel-angle-column sweep (diagnostics/inspect_metrology_phase1_sensitivity.py adapted: the steering input now perturbs the table's wheel-angle column +/-1 % instead of the ratio column, which production no longer reads; results in diagnostics/results_metrology_20261005/): no proportional flip within +/-1 %; both flips are different-mechanism jumps per the recorded exclusions (v3 C8 exit_4 ratio discontinuity, Dubai C1 apex_3); value retained. Author ruling 2026-10-05.]
